title: Indian Market News Brief — 24 Oct 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Higher crude oil prices and lower sales growth targets from major technology companies like Infosys may create pressure on the market. Strong quarterly earnings from automobile and banking companies like Tata Motors CV and IndusInd Bank may provide support. Investors are also watching high interest from buyers in major new public share offerings.

stories.headline: Infosys Q2 Results: Profit rises 6% YoY to Rs 7,823 crore; co lowers revenue guidance
stories.summary: Infosys reported a 6% increase in second-quarter net profit to ₹7,823 crore. However, the company cut its full-year sales growth target to 1-2% from 1.5-3%. Its American shares dropped over 6% following the news. The company declared an interim dividend of ₹26 per share.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower growth expectations for Infosys may create selling pressure on technology stocks.

stories.headline: Sensex today | Stock Market Highlights: Sensex, Nifty extend losses as crude surges to $114, all sectors close in red
stories.summary: Indian stock markets fell on Friday as crude oil prices surged to $114 per barrel. Benchmark index Nifty closed lower at 22,600 points. All major industry sectors ended the day with losses. Mid-cap and small-cap shares suffered their worst weekly drop in 20 months.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: High crude oil prices increase fuel and input costs for Indian companies, which can hurt overall corporate profits.

stories.headline: Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit
stories.summary: Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles division turned profitable with a net profit of ₹1,254 crore in the second quarter. This is a recovery from a net loss in the same period last year. Quarterly revenue jumped 37% to ₹23,930 crore. The company reported better truck demand and higher fleet usage.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong profit recovery and revenue growth in automobile stocks may boost trader confidence.

stories.headline: IndusInd Bank Q2 Results: Lender posts profit of Rs 1,176 crore vs Rs 445 crore loss a year ago
stories.summary: IndusInd Bank reported a net profit of ₹1,176 crore for the second quarter. This compares to a net loss of ₹445 crore recorded in the same quarter last year. Core interest income rose 4% year-on-year to ₹4,569 crore. Bad loans as a portion of total advances reduced to 2.73%.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Improved profitability and better loan recovery may support banking shares.

stories.headline: Jio IPO breaks 12 records: Rs 4.5 lakh crore bids, highest applications and more
stories.summary: Jio Platforms closed its public share offering with total demand reaching 22.19 times the shares on offer. The offering received over 1.25 crore applications and total bids exceeding ₹4.5 lakh crore. Institutional investors applied for 70.55 times their reserved share. Shares are set to list on October 28.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: High investor demand for large new listings shows strong buying interest in Indian markets.

stories.headline: India's 10-year bond falls for 10th week in record slump
stories.summary: Indian government bonds dropped for a tenth straight week, marking their longest weekly decline in thirty years. Rising crude oil prices and high central bank interest rates weighed on bond prices. The benchmark repo rate stands at 5.5%. Interest rates on 10-year government bonds rose to 7.47%.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher borrowing costs for government and businesses can slow economic activity and reduce corporate investment.

stories.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 profit jumps 59% YoY to Rs 3,677 crore on strong interest income, lower funding costs
stories.summary: Shriram Finance reported a 59.4% year-on-year increase in second-quarter profit to ₹3,677 crore. The gains were driven by higher interest income and lower borrowing costs. Total managed assets grew by 17%. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹6.50 per share.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong profit growth in large non-banking lenders can support financial sector stocks.

stories.headline: BPCL Q2 Results: Net profit declines 21% YoY to Rs 4,863 crore, revenue grows 29%
stories.summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation reported a 21.45% year-on-year fall in second-quarter profit to ₹4,863 crore. Total revenue grew nearly 30% to ₹1.28 lakh crore over the same period. Profit recovered compared to a loss in the previous quarter. The board approved plans for a new refinery in Andhra Pradesh.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Lower yearly profits could pressure refining shares, but strong revenue and quarterly recovery offer balance.

stories.headline: Dr Reddy’s Q2 Results: Net profit falls 36% YoY to Rs 913 crore, revenue declines marginally
stories.summary: Dr Reddy's Laboratories reported a 36% year-on-year fall in second-quarter profit to ₹913 crore. Total revenue declined 1.5% during the quarter. Weak sales in North America hurt overall performance. Sales growth in India and emerging markets helped reduce total losses.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower profits in major pharmaceutical companies can pull down healthcare stocks.

stories.headline: RBI governor reiterates listing requirement for top NBFCs as focus intensifies on Tata Sons
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India Governor stated that top-layer non-bank finance companies must list their shares on stock exchanges. The rule applies to major corporate holding companies including Tata Sons. The Governor did not name any single company directly. No extension to deadlines was announced.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Mandatory stock exchange listings could unlock asset value for holding companies, but timeline details remain uncertain.

stories.headline: Yes Bank AT1 bonds: Supreme Court overturns write-off, but will investors get coupon payments? What's the entire matter
stories.summary: The Supreme Court cancelled a previous write-off of Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds. Yes Bank stated it is unlikely to pay unpaid interest due this year. The bank plans to file a review petition against the order. Yes Bank warned its capital funds ratio could drop by about 2.5 percentage points.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower capital buffers and extra legal obligations can pressure banking stock prices.

stories.headline: Rupee little changed this week as oil-fueled declines wipe out early gains
stories.summary: The Indian rupee closed lower against the US dollar as crude oil prices rose to a five-month high. High oil costs raised worries about India's energy import bill. Technology stocks saw profit-taking as global investors moved into safer assets. The rupee settled near 94.93 against the US dollar.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: A weaker rupee combined with expensive crude oil increases import costs and inflation risks.
